;Arts and culture
*Bowing to pressure, [[France|French]] [[Publishing|publisher]] [[Éditions Gallimard|Gallimard]] suspends plans to reprint a [[compendium]] of "violently [[Antisemitism|antisemitic]] pamphlets" by novelist [[Louis-Ferdinand Céline]]. ;Business and economy
*[[Walmart employee wages]]
**[[Walmart]] announces that it will increase the [[minimum wage]] for its U.S. employees to $11 per hour and close 50 [[Sam's Club]] stores. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2018/01/11/walmart-boosts-minimum-wage-11-hands-out-bonuses-up-1-000-hourly-workers/1023606001/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Cryptocurrency#Legality|Legal status of cryptocurrency]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[Ministry of Justice (South Korea)|Ministry of Justice]] announces that it is a preparing a bill to ban [[cryptocurrency]] trading through exchanges. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-01-11/south-korea-flags-ban-cryptocurrency-trading-rattles-market/9322140 (ABC News Australia)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2018 Southern California mudflows]]
** The [[Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Office]] reports this afternoon that up to 43 people are still missing from Tuesday's [[mudslides]] as  rescuers continue to search through [[Montecito, California|Montecito’s]] massive debris field; this morning the report had been eight missing.  The casualty numbers are expected to  rise. [http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-mudslide-recovery-mainbar-20180111-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')]

;International relations
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] through the [[U.S. Justice Department]] establishes the Hezbollah Financing and Narcoterrorism Team to assist with the [[DEA]]'s [[Project Cassandra]] investigation into [[Funding of Hezbollah|groups supporting]] [[Hezbollah]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-hezbollah/attorney-general-sessions-sets-up-hezbollah-investigation-team-idUSKBN1F01V3 (Reuters)]
*[[United States–European Union relations]]
**The United Kingdom, France, and Germany call on [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] to endorse the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]. [http://www.france24.com/en/20180111-iran-nuclear-deal-eu-urges-trump (France 24)]

;Law and crime
*[[Media of the Philippines]]
**The [[Securities and Exchange Commission (Philippines)|Securities and Exchange Commission]] revokes the license of Rappler over its use of Philippine [[Depositary receipt|Depository Receipts]] (PDRs) issued to [[Omidyar Network]]. The commission ruled that the provisions of the PDRs issued by Rappler to Omidyar violates constitutional restrictions on foreign ownership and control of companies. Critics of the administration of President Rodrigo Duterte condemned the move as an "attack on press freedom". [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/companies/639728/sec-revokes-rappler-s-certificate-of-incorporation/story/ (GMA News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-media/philippine-regulator-revokes-news-sites-license-over-ownership-rules-media-outraged-idUSKBN1F40TE (Reuters)]
*[[Murder of Zainab Ansari]]
**The rape and murder of six-year-old girl Zainab in [[Pakistan]] has sparked outrage across the country. Two people die in protests in [[Kasur]] city. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1382243/6-year-old-zainabs-autopsy-suggests-child-endured-rape-captivity-before-murder (''Dawn'')]
*[[Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] passes a bill to reauthorize, for a period of six years, a key foreign intelligence collection program, permitted by [[Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 Amendments Act of 2008#Foreign surveillance|Section 702]]. Changes to the program will [[Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act#With a court order|require]] the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] to get a [[probable cause]] [[search warrant|warrant]] if it wants to view the contents of Americans' communications swept up in the [[Surveillance|process]]. [http://time.com/5099528/house-passes-spy-program-fisa/ (''Time'')]
*[[WikiLeaks]], [[Julian Assange#Political asylum and life at the Ecuadorian embassy|Julian Assange political asylum and life at the Ecuadorian embassy]]
**It is revealed that [[Ecuador]] granted citizenship to [[Julian Assange]]. Ecuador granted him [[Right of asylum|asylum]] in August 2012 and he has remained in the [[Embassy]] of Ecuador in [[London]] [[Assange v Swedish Prosecution Authority|avoiding]] [[extradition]] to [[Sweden]] on [[rape]] [[Criminal charge|charges]]. Subsequently, Swedish authorities dropped the charges in May 2017. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2018/jan/11/julian-assange-is-made-ecuadorian-citizen-in-effort-to-resolve-impasse (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Weinstein effect]]
**Twitter posts disseminate claims that actor [[Kirk Douglas]] (aged 101) had been accused in the past of having sexually assaulted actress [[Natalie Wood]] when she was 16 years old ({{circa|1954}}). [https://www.mediaite.com/online/twitter-calls-out-golden-globes-for-honoring-kirk-douglas-accused-of-raping-natalie-wood-not-a-good-look (Mediaite.com)]
*[[Murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner|1964 Murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner]]
**Former [[Ku Klux Klan]] organizer and convicted murderer [[Edgar Ray Killen]] dies in prison at the age of 92. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/01/12/obituaries/edgar-ray-killen-convicted-in-64-killings-of-rights-worker-dies-at-92.html ''(The New York Times)'']
